stem:
Polysaccharides, such as glycogen, are composed of thousands of monomers.

Oligosaccharides are carbohydrates that contain three to ten monomers in their chain.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Nystose is one example of an oligosaccharide. The structure of nystose is shown in Fig. 6.1.

{{figure:figure_6_1.webp}}

Fig. 6.1

State **three** differences between the structures of nystose and glycogen, **other** than the number of monomers in the molecules.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Cells use oligosaccharides to synthesise glycoproteins, which are transported to cell surface membranes.

Describe the roles of the rough endoplasmic reticulum and the Golgi body in synthesising glycoproteins.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: State **one** role of glycoproteins in the cell surface membrane.
